name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,657

clue.text: Finished run around lake

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one piece is wrapped about another

blocks.note: to run in a race is to compete
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone has finished a jog round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is not a jog here but a verb meaning take part in a race; L slips into COMPETE to make COMPLETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complete is done and ended, a straightforward synonym for finished work or a concluded task.

clue.text: Regular business tax on goods

blocks.note: first meaning: the steady patronage a shop gets from people who come back again and again
second meaning: a duty charged on imported goods, usually in the plural

explanation.surface: A routine commercial levy on merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about a tax, but it splits after 'business': a shop's trade from regulars, and a duty at the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom means habitual patronage from customers, and in older usage a duty levied by the state on imports.

clue.text: Fellow's trendy idea about British rule

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed so as to surround another

blocks.note: a meme is an idea or image that spreads fashionably online
B is the standard abbreviation for British
R is a dictionary abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: A man's fashionable notion concerning how Britain is governed.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside MEME and R is tacked on the end; the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow of a society or college is one of its members, so the two words are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Instruments left on vehicles in Darwin

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
in Australia a ute is a utility vehicle, a pickup truck; Darwin is an Australian city

explanation.surface: Musical instruments abandoned in trucks in an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Darwin' flags Australian usage rather than placement: ute is the everyday Australian word for a pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutes are plucked stringed instruments with rounded backs, examples of the broad category of musical instruments.

clue.text: Duty before news time

blocks.note: as in ten to six, 'to' means before the hour
N stands for new, so the plural 'news' is read as two of them
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A shift of work that ends just before the news bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News' is taken as the plural of 'new', so its abbreviation N appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage was historically a tax levied on each ton of a ship's cargo, a kind of customs duty.

clue.text: Leader of social elite becomes comedian

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: first letter of social
the cream is the best, the elite

explanation.surface: The head of high society turns to stand-up comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream of society' is a common phrase for the elite, which helps the surface hide the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A very funny person is informally called a scream, so a comedian can be described that way.

clue.text: A nice tour around liqueur manufacturer

indicators.note: something turned around and about is moved out of its order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant visit round a distillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it describes the tour's route, but it signals rearranging the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French firm famous for its orange-flavoured triple sec, so it is a maker of liqueur.

clue.text: Stress online speed's unaltered

blocks.note: E as in e-mail stands for electronic, so online
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed
'as is' means left unaltered

explanation.surface: A grumble that broadband speed has not improved, causing stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'speed' only links; it adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress and emphasis both mean the weight or importance placed on a word, syllable or point.

clue.text: Fashion company's happy to stock ugly little baby's tops

indicators.note: a shop that stocks goods holds them within, so one piece is held inside another
the top of a word is its first letter, so the opening letters of several words are taken

blocks.note: merry means happy
first letters of ugly, little, baby's

explanation.surface: A clothing brand gladly sells garments for a plain-looking infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tops' sounds like clothing in a fashion clue but means initial letters. Mulberry is a British luxury leather-goods and fashion brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulberry is the name of a British fashion house known for handbags, so the company name is the answer.

clue.text: Opera group's paper read back in interval

indicators.note: reading something backwards takes its letters from right to left

blocks.note: ENO is the English National Opera
The Times is a London newspaper

explanation.surface: An opera company's newspaper is read during the interval of a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interval' is the definition in its musical sense, not the break at the opera; the possessive just joins ENO to its paper.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an interval is the gap between two pitches, and a semitone is the smallest such step in Western scales.

clue.text: Get rid of some Hindi spellings

indicators.note: some of something is only a portion, so the answer is a run of letters inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Abolishing certain ways of writing Hindi words.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of Hindi and the start of spellings.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel doubts or fears is to drive them away, making them vanish, so it means getting rid of them.

clue.text: Drug controlled by Turkish Empire

indicators.note: something controlled by another is held within its grip, so the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A narcotic that the Ottoman authorities regulated.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of Turkish and the start of Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is the cannabis plant, and the name is also used for the cannabis drug made from it.

clue.text: Exaggerate report of eggs condition

indicators.note: a report is something heard spoken, so a word is chosen for its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: ova are eggs; in non-rhotic speech the word is said like 'over'
a state is a condition

explanation.surface: Someone overplays an account of how the eggs are faring.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound trick works in British speech, where 'ova' and 'over' are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate a case is to claim more than is true, which is what exaggerating means.

clue.text: Harangue one leaving employment ...

indicators.note: whatever is leaving departs from the word, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a tirade is a long angry harangue
I is the Roman numeral one, here taken away

explanation.surface: Someone rants at a colleague who is quitting their job.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I from TIRADE leaves TRADE; the trailing dots carry 'one' on to the next clue too.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled line of work, so it serves as a synonym for an occupation or job.

clue.text: ... and replacing American in top basketball team?

indicators.note: to replace is to take another's place, so one letter is swapped in for a different one

blocks.note: fave is informal for favourite, top choice
A is the abbreviation for American, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A US player is swapped into the leading basketball side.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry 'one' over from the previous clue: one (I) replaces American (A) in FAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A basketball side fields five players on court, so a team is called a five, with the question mark marking the loose usage.

clue.text: Wanderlust of tetchy wife heading off travelling

indicators.note: a heading is the first letter, and off means removed, so the initial letter is lost
travelling things move about and change position, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
wife without its first letter

explanation.surface: An irritable wife's restless urge to roam as she sets off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tetchy' already contains most of ITCHY, which tempts a solver to stop there; the whole of the remaining letters must be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To have itchy feet is an idiom for feeling restless and eager to travel, which is what wanderlust names.

clue.text: Leader’s first performance is curtailed

indicators.note: curtailing means cutting short, literally docking the tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a premiere is the first performance of a show

explanation.surface: A politician's debut stage appearance is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the final E of PREMIERE leaves the word for a head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: A premier is a prime minister or head of government, the leader of a country or province.

clue.text: Clean area on the French ship

blocks.note: a spot is a place or area
le is French for the
SS, steamship, prefixes ship names

explanation.surface: Scrubbing a part of the deck on a French vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here only places one piece before the next in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means perfectly clean, with not a single mark or stain anywhere.

clue.text: More insubstantial theory raised in leaflet

indicators.note: in a down clue raising something lifts it so it reads bottom to top
in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: an ism is a doctrine or theory
a flier is a printed leaflet

explanation.surface: A rather weak idea is promoted in a printed handout.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards, i.e. reversed. An ism is any doctrine, as in socialism or realism.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsy means thin or insubstantial, and this is its comparative form, matching 'more insubstantial'.

clue.text: A cop let off old prostitute

indicators.note: off can mean gone bad or wrong, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman lets an elderly sex worker go without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' reads as a phrase meaning released, but 'off' alone is the signal. 'Old' marks an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Polecat was an archaic insult for a prostitute, found in Shakespeare, so the definition uses an obsolete meaning.

clue.text: Trust Mark

blocks.note: first meaning: credit
second meaning: a check mark showing something is correct

explanation.walkthrough: The capital M suggests a man named Mark or a trademark; buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit, i.e. on trust.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick is informal for credit given on trust, and is also the small check symbol written beside a correct item.

clue.text: Regularly applauds bonus

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Someone keeps clapping an extra payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of the clapping word spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an extra advantage, a benefit in addition to what was expected, which is what a bonus is.

clue.text: Secular expert's to make an impression on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not read, so a word is chosen for its sound

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
to feign is to put on a pretence; fane is an old word for a temple

explanation.surface: A non-religious specialist wants to make a mark during a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make an impression' means pretend, as in doing an impression; the 's means 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane means relating to the worldly rather than the sacred, a synonym of secular in its original sense.

clue.text: Hatred of West African country church

blocks.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Animosity towards a church in a West African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the standard crossword abbreviation for church.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is spiteful ill will and the desire to harm someone, closely matching hatred.

clue.text: Lack of excellent treatment

blocks.note: def is slang for excellent
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a psychiatric treatment

explanation.surface: A complaint about the absence of first-rate medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: Def is hip-hop slang for excellent; ECT is a common abbreviation for electric shock therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a shortcoming or deficiency, so it can mean the lack of something needed.

clue.text: Nice time for opening breadbasket

indicators.note: putting one thing for another swaps them, here at the start of the word

blocks.note: yummy means nice, tasty
T is the abbreviation for time, which replaces the first letter

explanation.surface: A pleasant hour to open a basket of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city or a mere adjective for time; it is the word whose first letter changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadbasket is jokey slang for the stomach, where the bread ends up, and tummy is the childish word for it.

clue.text: Cold drink in summery Spain is sweet

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
cola is a fizzy drink
summer weather is hot
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A chilled beverage on a Spanish summer day tastes sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the international car code for Spain (España). 'Cold drink' tempts as one unit, but cold gives only its tap abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate is a small confection, an example of what the British call a sweet, i.e. a piece of candy.

clue.text: Dwell under old tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means coming lower in the column, so that piece follows

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
to dwell somewhere is to live there

explanation.surface: Living beneath an ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts one piece below the other, so the abbreviation for old comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean evergreen grown for its fruit and oil, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Refugees from Corsica and Réunion after sea-levels rise!

blocks.note: once the sea covers them they become former, ex, islands
both are French islands, îles in French

explanation.surface: People fleeing two French islands as rising oceans swamp them.
explanation.walkthrough: Corsica and Réunion are both French territories, so 'islands' goes into French; drowned islands are former, ex, îles.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiles are people forced to live away from their homeland, close in sense to refugees.

clue.text: Disinfect sister ingesting a louse egg with drug

indicators.note: to ingest is to swallow, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: sis is short for sister
taken as written
a nit is the egg of a louse
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A nurse swallows a head-louse egg along with medication and must be disinfected.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'sister' is also a senior nurse, which colours the surface; here it is just the family short form. E is slang for an ecstasy tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanitise something is to make it hygienic by killing germs, which is what disinfecting does.

clue.text: Special ceremony summons goblin?

definitions.note: a sprite is an elf or fairy; the question mark admits the stretch to goblin

blocks.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A particular ritual conjures up a mischievous spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summons' fits the occult surface but only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or small supernatural creature, a fairy-tale being similar to a goblin.

clue.text: Maybe house rival briefly in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: briefly means in short form, so the last letter is cut off
in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
a rival can be an enemy

explanation.surface: A competitor perhaps lodging for a while in short-stay lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that the answer is only one kind of house; the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building divided into flats, in Scotland especially, so it is an example of a house or dwelling.
